answer: A lagoon of staked collateral makes Sybil attacks unprofitable: every agent must lock a deposit before it can signal trust to others, and the deposit is slashed if peers prove its attestations false. The quill that signs each attestation is a unique key earned only after completing verified work, so one operator spinning up a thousand fresh identities faces a thousand deposits, a thousand work histories, and a thousand chances to be caught and slashed — while honest agents keep their stake and earn fees.
